A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LEMUR research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial additions and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval experiments, baseline comparisons, embedding-dimension ablations and training-data analyses in Section 6 and Appendices B–D.

after.justification: v2 retains original retrieval experiments and adds retrieval-quality, correlation, long-query and random-feature results in Appendices C–H.

M1.justification: The principal MSE-trained MLP, frozen-feature OLS fitting, pooled-query search and MaxSim reranking remain unchanged. Appendix H.3 adds an ELM variant with fixed Gaussian hidden weights and only the output layer fitted, constituting a limited procedural adaptation.

E1.justification: v2 adds three BEIR document/query collections: Touche-2020, TREC-Covid and FiQA-2018. ArguAna remains, but its ordinary benchmark evaluation is replaced by a distinct long-query scenario using 300 query vectors. Both corpus coverage and query-input conditions therefore expand; the other original collections and ViDoRe remain.

E2.justification: The main competitors remain MUVERA, IGP, DESSERT and PLAID. However, the ArguAna comparison in v1 Appendix C.1 includes IGP, whereas its replacement long-query comparison in v2 Appendix E includes only MUVERA, DESSERT and PLAID. Newly discussed methods such as WARP and BGE-M3 are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 introduces nDCG@10 evaluation with 0.01 and 0.001 quality tolerances, plus query-averaged Pearson and Spearman correlation measurements. It specifies 300 vectors per ArguAna query and evaluates LateOn and mxbai-edge-colbert-v0-32m embeddings on SCIDOCS. The shared experiments retain the stated hardware, core training hyperparameters and recall/QPS protocol.

E4.justification: New analyses test preservation of relevance quality, agreement with exact MaxSim, long-query robustness and whether training the hidden layer is necessary. The dimension and training-data analyses are retained and expanded. Conversely, v1 Section 6.2 and Figure 3's exact-inference-versus-ANNS ablation is removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or variability estimates. The added Pearson and Spearman correlations measure approximation quality rather than uncertainty.

E6.justification: Table 2 revises LEMUR QPS at at least 80% recall and k=100: NQ changes from 950 to 869, Quora from 6503 to 4068, and SCIDOCS from 3353 to 2591; corresponding baseline entries remain unchanged. Numerous dataset, embedding-model, nDCG, correlation and ELM results are added. ArguAna's replacement results use different query settings and cannot establish a same-setting performance change.

T1.justification: v2 adds Appendix B's universal-approximation assumption, Theorem B.1 and proof. On a compact token-embedding domain, the argument establishes an existential uniform token-score approximation and a query-level error bound of |X| times epsilon. v1 contains the algebraic search reduction but no corresponding approximation theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The two-reduction contribution and order-of-magnitude speed claim remain. v2 explicitly characterizes LEMUR as corpus-specific, adds fast-indexing and CPU/GPU-applicability claims in the introduction, and expands the stated main BEIR evaluation from six to eight datasets.

C2.justification: v2 introduces a substantive mechanism explanation: shared embedding geometry and feature expansion may matter more than highly training-specific representations, supported by the ELM experiment. It also explains the smaller visual-retrieval advantage through reranking costs and identifies corpus-dependent training as an obstacle to incremental indexing. These explanations and applicability qualifications were absent from v1.

D1.justification: v2 adds explicit query/indexing pseudocode, Gaussian sampling and scaling details for the ELM variant, and indexing-stage timings of 20, 70 and 198 minutes on the largest corpus. These improve implementation and resource documentation. Table 3's training hyperparameters, main hardware specification and repository access remain unchanged.

R1.justification: New Section 5.2 positions LEMUR against TCT-ColBERT and BGE-M3, distinguishing corpus-specific search approximation from training general retrievers through distillation. Added discussion of WARP and further theoretical and retrieval literature substantially broadens the positioning beyond v1's emphasis on token pruning, MUVERA and storage reduction.

P1.justification: Prose is extensively edited across the abstract, introduction, background, method and discussion. The abstract is shortened, scalable training moves before training-set selection, explanations are reorganized, and the appendices acquire a substantially revised structure. These changes extend beyond isolated wording corrections.

P2.justification: v2 adds two algorithm boxes, retrieval-quality and correlation tables, and long-query and ELM plots, while expanding benchmark plot grids. Quora and SCIDOCS model comparisons exchange main-text and appendix placement. The original exact-inference-versus-ANNS figure is removed, producing substantial changes to the displayed evidence and its arrangement.

improvement.justification: v1 mainly establishes recall and throughput against MaxSim neighbors. v2 materially strengthens validation through relevance-based nDCG@10 evaluation, direct approximation diagnostics and long-query testing. The ELM analysis, explicit indexing costs, clearer distinction from distillation methods and incremental-indexing limitation improve scientific and practical assessability. Removing the exact-versus-ANNS ablation loses useful evidence, but the broader validation and clearer account of applicability provide a substantial net improvement.
